meta.note: 29 shots: bin/dissect found 28; its shot 6 holds a hidden cut inside a white sun-flash (now shots 6 and 7, cut at 16.665), and its S21/S22 boundary is moved from 41.23 (lights coming on) to the real cut at 40.889. Shots 8-29 are dissect's 7-28. All shot times are frame-exact (first frame of each shot, from frame differences; dissect's rounded times run 1-3 frames late). Frame k of the source is at k * 12/287 s (23.917 fps).

acts.name: The ask
acts.function: Hook. Dawn over the farm, then the porch at golden hour: the old farmer says it may be time to retire; his grown daughter answers 'How about one last time? Together.' Almost no music: dialogue and room tone.

acts.name: The last season
acts.function: The song enters on the cut to the field. Planting to harvest, father and daughter side by side, intercut with her childhood on the same farm through then/now pairs (planting: a white sun-flash into the memory; tailgate snack with {BRAND}: same two, same pose, decades apart; the card she drew him, now taped in his cab). Ends at harvest with a potato held up to the sky and the loaded truck.

acts.name: The surprise
acts.function: 'One more thing.' She leads him into the dark barn; the lights snap on to a retirement party for him.

acts.name: The handover
acts.function: Night, back on the same porch (bookend of act 1, same over-the-shoulder setups): he presses the farm keys into her hand, 'It's your farm now.', she breaks into tears and they hug. Wide of the porch, the old dog at their feet, the super about generations of farmers.

acts.name: End card
acts.function: Golden-hour aerial over the crop rows: {BRAND} badge, {TAGLINE}, {SUBLINE}; the song's final chord rings out.

look.grade: natural, filmic, warm; earth browns, denim blues and creams; skin warm and true. Present day is clean and contrasty; memories (shots 7-10, 12, 16) are warmer and softer, with hazy cream skies and a honey-rust palette (saturated warm soil, gentle contrast). No stylised teal-orange, no added haze.

text_style.diegetic: Only one piece of text lives in the picture: the hand-painted banner 'HAPPY RETIREMENT' in the barn (shot 23, not in either cut). Licence plates and the child's card are drawn in the scene, never as graphics.

sound.music: One song carries the film: a slow, intimate piano-and-voice cover of a 2000s indie-pop ballad about returning to a shared place, sung by a soft female voice, ~85 bpm and rubato (the beat drifts 0.63-0.86 s; bar about 2.8 s). It is set/score.wav, the film's own soundtrack with the spoken lines removed (vocal/music separation; the singer stays in, the dialogue is cut out of the vocal stem where it stands alone). The keys jingle (5.40-6.20) sits in the score.

sound.downbeats: measured (librosa beat track + chord change): 1.46 2.22 2.91 ... 13.55 14.33 ... 24.71 ... 30.59 33.08 35.84 ... 47.29 49.96 52.73 53.48 ... 57.04. bin/template beats reports 172.25 bpm (double time) on a fixed grid that drifts up to 0.3 s from the real downbeats in this rubato ballad; the cuts join the score on the measured beats.
sound.speech: Six spoken lines, all diegetic and close-miked, no narrator. Father: L01, L02 (heard over the aerial, the porch wide and the keys: his face is never readable while he says them), L04 and L06 on camera. Daughter: L03 on camera, L05 on camera at the cut. Lines are never under music in act 1; in acts 3-4 they sit in gaps of the song.
sound.mix: Dialogue dry, intimate, no reverb, at about -24 to -30 dB RMS (peaks -7 to -16 dBFS); the score under it in act 1 is 15-30 dB lower. From 13.9 the song is the bed at -24 to -30 LUFS momentary; it never ducks. No sound effects beyond the keys jingle and natural room tone: no wind, no footsteps, no crowd noise from the party.

char_father.fixes: The farmer, an invented man ~72 (not a likeness of anyone): 1.80 m, lean, broad slightly stooped shoulders, big work-worn hands; bald crown with close-cropped white hair at the sides; full short white beard and moustache; weathered tanned fair skin; warm brown eyes; gentle wry half-smile. Wardrobe sheet, left to right: (1) porch day, shots 2-5: tan-brown duck-canvas chore jacket with brown corduroy collar over a navy-blue plaid flannel shirt, jeans; (2) planting, shot 6: faded navy denim chore jacket, navy cap, tan leather gloves; (3) tailgate, shot 11: charcoal flannel work shirt, grey-navy mesh-back trucker cap, brown canvas trousers; (4) night porch, shots 25-28: dark charcoal-brown waxed jacket with brown corduroy cuffs over a cream henley, sage-green knit scarf. Harvest (shot 18): outfit 1 jacket with a cap. Wedding ring on his left hand.

char_daughter.fixes: The daughter, an invented woman ~42: 1.68 m, slim and strong; light olive skin, faint freckles; dark-brown hair in a low loose ponytail with face-framing strands; dark-brown eyes, straight brows; small gold studs; no makeup. Wardrobe sheet: (1) porch day, shots 2-5: off-white canvas chore jacket with brown corduroy collar over a dark navy top; (2) planting, shot 6: black-navy work jacket, navy cap with the ponytail through it, tan gloves; (3) tailgate, shot 11: cream button-up work shirt, jeans, tan boots; (4) harvest and night, shots 18-19, 25-28: rust-brown canvas chore jacket (knit cuffs) over a blue denim shirt (a dark cap at harvest).

char_young_father.fixes: The farmer in the memories (~35), derived from char_father so the face carries across 37 years: thick dark-brown hair, short full dark-brown beard. Wardrobe: (left) planting memory, shot 7: worn tan canvas jacket over a brown shirt, brown cap; (right) tailgate memory, shot 10: teal short-sleeved shirt open over a grey tee, khaki trousers, olive-tan trucker cap.

char_girl.fixes: The daughter at ~6, derived from char_daughter: light olive skin, dark-brown chin-length bob with straight bangs, big brown eyes. Wardrobe: (left) planting memory, shot 7: mustard-yellow hooded rain jacket, brown trousers, bright yellow rubber boots, small yellow gloves; (right) tailgate memory, shot 10: brown canvas bib overalls over a navy-white striped tee.

char_dog.fixes: The family golden retriever: a pale cream-gold 10-week puppy in the memories (shot 10, in the girl's arms); the same dog at 12 with a deep golden-red coat and white-grey muzzle in the present (shot 11 in the truck bed on a striped dog bed; shot 28 lying at their feet).

product_bag.fixes: The {BRAND} snack bag (default generic design): pillow foil bag ~28 x 20 cm, glossy golden yellow (#F2C200), crimped seals; white rounded-rectangle label with 'POTATO CHIPS' in bold dark-brown rounded capitals and a small green sprout; a chip photo under it; a dark-green bottom band. In his palm on the porch (shot 3) and pressed into her hand at night (shot 25): the story's prop.

slots.{BRAND}: the snack brand: its bag (product_bag, shots 10-11) and its badge on the end card. Default: a generic yellow bag reading 'POTATO CHIPS' and a cream oval sprout badge.
slots.{PRODUCT}: what the family's crop becomes (default: potato chips). The crop itself (potatoes, product_potato) can change with it: apples for cider, wheat for bread, grapes for wine; then the fields, the pulled plant and the raised produce change too.
slots.{SUPER}: the two-line super on the night porch wide. Default: 'Real potatoes grown by generations' / 'of farmers.'
slots.{TAGLINE}: end card line 1. Default: 'Grown by families. Made for yours.'
slots.{SUBLINE}: end card line 2. Default: 'Made from real potatoes.'
slots.{LEGAL}: end card fine print. Default: placeholder text.
slots.{PARENT_LOGO}: optional corner mark on the end card (top right). Default: none.
slots.cast: father (~70s) and grown daughter (~40s), their younger selves (~35 and ~6), the family dog at two ages. Keep the ages: the film is about one generation handing on to the next.
slots.places: a family farm: house with a porch, fields at planting and harvest, a barn and yard. Any crop.
slots.lines: L01-L06 can be rewritten, keeping each line's length (count syllables; a generated read runs 10-20% slower, so write shorter) and the two-beat structure: he hints at stopping, she asks for one last season together; at the end he hands it over in four words.
slots.music: a soft cover of a well-known ballad about a shared place, female voice, piano-led, ~85 bpm. A new film may license its own; keep the arc: silence under the ask, entry on the cut to the field, a gap for the handover line, the last phrase on the wide, the final chord on the end card.

cast_notes: All people in the set are invented (text-to-image), never likenesses of the actors. The young father and the girl are derived from the adult sheets so that faces carry across the years.
